Tara: Heads-up — since yesterday's gpu-kernel roll we have a regressed memory-pressure pattern on the t4 pool. OOMs spiked and kv cache fragmentation jumped. Quick profiler dump below:
```
profile snapshot (20:12 UTC):
  total_kv_slots=3.2M -> 3.1M
  kv_slots_free=1.2M -> 600k
  fragmentation_ratio=0.42 -> 0.74
  kv_hitrate=0.63 -> 0.51
  p50 latency +8ms, p95 +35ms, p99 +120ms
  OOM_count (3h)=2 -> 14
```
The timing correlates with the kernel change that altered slab alignment and the keyhash variant. Need quick triage: is this allocation fragmentation, key variance, or eviction/TTL interaction?

sre-bot: Alert: mempressure OOM spike observed 2026-03-16T03:14Z — 28/30 hosts flagged in t4-pool (auto-created ticket INF-4321).

Vikram: I ran a focused microprof on a repro host. Findings: allocation churn is highest at small object sizes (<=128B). The new kernel reduced header padding which ironically increased bin scattering for our prefix-length distribution. Also saw a ~12% increase in unique key variants caused by un-normalized prompt whitespace (users with trailing spaces).

Vikram: Two quick mitigations we can test: canonicalize cache keys (trim/normalize whitespace + collapse repeated spaces) and a "soft-trim" eviction that preferentially drops tiny/single-use prefixes before large shared KV entries.

Leah: Sketch of soft-trim config (proposal):
```yaml
soft_trim_v1:
  target_free_pct: 0.12          # aim to keep ~12% free slots on GPU-side cache
  eviction_priority:
    - small_prefix_first       # evict small fixed-size entries before large ones
    - least_recent
    - low_access_weight        # entries with <2 accesses in last 10m
  batch_eviction_window_ms: 50  # evict in small batches to avoid latency spikes
  prefetch_rewarm: true        # allow controlled rewarm for hot prefixes only
```
Leah: This avoids wholesale LRU sweeps and reduces fragmentation pressure.

Mike: Batcher changes I can ship alongside: cap max_prefix_length to 512 when forming kernel batches (prevents huge unique prefixes from scattering), and add a coalescing preference in the batcher to group requests that share the same normalized key. Also add a short defer (3 requests) before auto-prefill of unseen small prefixes so we don't fill the cache with one-offs.

Vikram: If we canonicalize keys we should also add a small key-hash metric so we can monitor collision/hitrate impact. Proposed A/B: canonicalize + soft_trim_v1 + batch cap on 5% canary of t4 pool. Metrics to watch: kv_hitrate, fragmentation_ratio, p99 latency, OOM_count, rewarm_rate. Run minimum 6h. Success criteria: kv_hitrate >= 0.6 and OOM_count down >50%.

Tara: I can own the canary rollout. Please add a trace tag "soft-trim-v1" and enable verbose kv stats on the canary hosts so we can filter. @mike can you add the tag in the request metadata? :thumbsup:

Mike: Yep — I'll add the trace tag and push batcher cap to the canary config. I'll also expose a metric kv_key_variants_per_min to see if canonicalization helps.

Leah: I'll push soft_trim_v1 to staging and run a synthetic workload that mimics the tail-of-prefix distribution for 2 hours tonight. I'll post the staging graphs.

Vikram: Small note — we should instrument slab allocator per-size-bin fragmentation. If soft_trim reduces fragmentation we should see freed_slots increase evenly across small bins.

Tara: Decision items: (1) canary with canonicalize + soft_trim_v1 + batch cap @5% t4; (2) add trace tag and kv metrics; (3) staging synthetic run; (4) rollback plan if p99 rises >25% or OOMs don't improve after 2h.

sre-bot: Ticket INF-4321 updated: assigned to @tara, priority P1 until canary results.

Leah: +1
Vikram: ack
Mike: on it, will announce canary start in #eng-releases when deployed.
Tara: Thanks — I'll coordinate validation and call rollback if thresholds breach.
